title: Group antenatal care and attendance at recommended contacts: a cost-effectiveness analysis for a six-hub maternity service
subtitle: Economic evaluation of offering group care across community hubs
statement: Two of six community hubs have offered group antenatal care since January 2025, where fewer than half of women previously attended the eight recommended contacts. The trust board will decide in 2027 whether to offer it in all hubs, and needs the cost for each additional woman attending her recommended contacts compared with individual care, with honest uncertainty.
whoAffected: Pregnant women booked at the six hubs, especially women under 20, women new to the country and women with a previous loss; midwives; the trust board and finance team.
whatHurts: Missed antenatal contacts, which can mean missed screening and late recognition of problems, concentrated in groups already at higher risk.
currentPractice: Individual appointments in four hubs; a choice of group or individual care in two hubs since January 2025.
whyNow: The board decides on extension in 2027 and the finance team has offered analyst time now.
constraints: No new data collection from women; existing booking, attendance, rota and invoice data only; about 60 hours of finance analyst time; the report is due to the trust board in March 2027.
patientCenteredGoal: Every pregnant woman attends the care she needs in a form she can use.
summary: Problem framed as a cost-effectiveness question about offering group care.
